samples.summary: The entry-parity guard test was not extended with './model/table-nesting.js', so the exact bug this delta fixes stays untested
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/store/entry-parity.test.ts` exists precisely to catch "exported from the browser entry only" regressions (its header cites `normalizeListLevel` taking the integration suites down at import time). Its `it.each` allowlist names block-helpers, model/types, list-level, row-height and numeric-attrs — but not `./model/table-nesting.js`. The delta adds `export { MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH } from './model/table-nesting.js';` to `packages/docs/src/node.ts:145` without adding the matching allowlist row, so nothing in the unit lane asserts the Node entry re-exports it; deleting the new line again would leave every docs/frontend vitest suite green and only blow up at module-load time in the Yorkie integration lane. Searched: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH repo-wide, read entry-parity.test.ts in full.

samples.summary: The YorkieDocStore nesting cap (the Node-side reader this export exists for) has no test covering the truncation behavior
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:478-480` bounds its table descent with `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` — the consumer whose Node-side import failure motivated this delta. `packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts` covers only the `docsTreeToDocument`/`treeNodeToBlock` twin and `computeTableLayout`; grep for `nesting|NESTING|depth` under packages/frontend/tests/app/docs finds no test of the store's cap (the only 'nested table' hit, yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3262, inserts a 2x2 table and asserts row count — unrelated to depth). So a regression in the store's guard (off-by-one, wrong constant, or removing the cap and re-introducing the stack overflow on document open) would ship green. Guard code predates this delta, but this delta is what makes the constant nameable there.
